newsitem.title: USA: U.S. carrier may leave leave Gulf next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carrier may leave leave Gulf next week.

text.p: The United States is planning to remove the aircraft carrier Carl Vinson from the Gulf next week, leaving only the carrier Enterprise in the waterway near Iraq, a U.S. defence official said on Tuesday.

"Barring unforseen circumstances, the tentative plan is to take it (the Vinson) out next week," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters. Defence Secretary William Perry said last week that Iraq was "backing off" from a recent confrontation with Washington.

The move of the Vinson, scheduled to return to its home port in Bremerton, Washington, after six months at sea, would leave the Enterprise in the key waterway to watch over southern Iraq. An announcement of the move is expected by the Pentagon this week.

The Enterprise was moved to the Gulf two weeks ago from the Adriatic to join the Vinson in a regional U.S. military buildup after Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's forces attacked Kurds in northern Iraq and Iraqi missiles were fired at U.S. warplanes policing "no-fly" zones over northern and southern Iraq.

Iraq at first vowed to keep shooting missiles at U.S. and allied aircraft, but later promised to halt such attacks, which followed a strike by U.S. air- and sea-launched cruise missiles against air defence targets in southern Iraq.

Perry told reporters travelling with him on a trip to Nordic countries last week that a decision would be made this week on whether to remove the Vinson from the Gulf. He said the military situation in the region had calmed from the tense confrontation earlier in September.

"All of the evidence that I've seen in the last four or five days is positive," he said. "I do truly believe that Iraq is backing off the threatening actions they were taking a week ago, but we will watch it very carefully, very carefully, every day, every hour."

But senior U.S. offcials said nearly 3,500 American troops, flown to Kuwait for manoeuvres during the crisis, were likely to remain for in the emirate for two months to train with some 1,200 U.S. soldiers who were already there.

Iraq announced its conciliatory move on the anti-aircraft missiles after the United States also deployed a squadron of eight F-117A stealth fighters to Kuwait and stationed heavy B-52 bombers at a British air base on the island of Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean.
Perry said last week that the United States currently had no intention of moving additional military forces to the region.
